result: I tested 3 properties on `lxml_html_clean.clean` and found one real bug: a crash in `Cleaner` when `host_whitelist` is set. **The bug (Crash, Medium severity).** If `host_whitelist` is set, one malformed URL in an `') # ValueError: Invalid IPv6 URL ``` `https://[evil]/` fails the same way. The cause is in `allow_embedded_url` (`clean.py:536`): it calls `urllib.parse.urlsplit`, which raises `ValueError` on bad bracketed hosts, and nothing catches it. So anyone who can submit HTML can make sanitization fail for any app that uses `host_whitelist`, the documented way to allow things like YouTube iframes. An app that catches errors broadly might then fall back to the unsanitized HTML. The default cleaner never calls `urlsplit`, so it isn't affected. **Fix.** Catch the `ValueError` from `urlsplit` and `.hostname` and treat that URL as not allowed. I tried this with a temporary patch at runtime, without editing the library file. The malformed iframe was then removed and `https://trusted.com/v` was still kept. **Properties that passed (1,000 generated examples each):** - **Host whitelist matching:** a URL was never allowed unless the host a browser would actually use was `trusted.com`. I checked this against a small browser-style URL parser, with tricks like backslashes, `@`, extra slashes, `%2f` and uppercase schemes. - **Default sanitizer:** across random nested HTML (svg, math, style, noscript, template, base, ``, encoded `javascript:` and `data:` URLs), nothing survived cleaning: no `
